title: Level 1 Mastery Check
goal: Confirm the learner reads and spells real CVC words and pseudowords at ≥90%, knows all 26 letter-sounds, all 24 heart words, and reliably tells apart b/d/p/q — the Level 1 exit gate.
newToday: nothing new — this session administers the full instrument.
heartLine: cumulative review only (all 24, no new ones).
time: 20–30 minutes, can be split across two short sessions if needed (this is a test session, not a teaching one — fatigue affects the score, so don't push through if the learner is visibly tired).

listen.title: You Did Something Real
listen.passage: Fourteen lessons ago, this course started with three sounds and a handful of made-up "alien words." Today's check uses every single letter in English, a spelling rule, a plural ending, and twenty-four words that don't even follow the normal rules — and asks for all of it back, cold, without any warm-up hints. That's not a small ask. Whatever the score turns out to be, getting through fourteen full lessons of new material, in order, each one building on the last, is real, durable progress — the kind that doesn't disappear the way a memorized page would. What comes next, in Level 2, isn't starting over; it's the exact same skill, aimed at bigger and bigger words.

tier2.def: lasting a long time without wearing out or disappearing.
tier2.full: lasting a long time without wearing out or disappearing. "A durable skill doesn't fade the way a memorized fact does." "These boots are durable enough for years of work." Your turn: name something in your life that's durable.

questions: What does the passage say is different about a "durable" skill compared to a memorized page?
How does the passage describe what Level 2 will be, compared to Level 1?
